summary.headline: Orders and revenue both finished behind target at 98.4% and 89.6%; the quarter stands at 87.7% of target with cancellations notably higher.

points.what: Orders came in at 789, up 13.4% week on week and 98.4% of the weekly target of 802.
points.so_what: Double-digit order growth was still not enough to close the week's gap to target.

points.what: Revenue was $53,365, 89.6% of target, a gap of $6,220.
points.so_what: Revenue fell further short of target than orders did, so the week's miss sits in value per order rather than order count.

points.what: The cancellation rate rose 4.2 pp to 19.0%, a change the brief marks as notable and bad.
points.so_what: With each percentage point of cancellations worth $659 of revenue, this rise worked against the week's revenue attainment.

points.what: New customer signups rose 28.7% to 287, also marked as notable.
points.so_what: This was the fastest-growing weekly measure, running ahead of order growth of 13.4%.

points.what: The cancellation rate of 19.0% is 5.4 pp above the same week last year, rated bad on both the weekly and yearly comparison.
points.so_what: Cancellations are elevated on both timeframes, which is a live risk to revenue attainment in the remaining weeks of the quarter.

points.what: Year-to-date revenue is 87.7% of target, and hitting the full-year target of $3,888,802 requires $77,189 a week against a recent eight-week pace of $51,914.
points.so_what: The required pace sits far above what the business has been running, so the full-year target is out of reach at the current rate.

points.what: Orders grew 58.1% and revenue 49.0% year on year, against the 75.0% growth the targets assume.
points.so_what: Growth is real but below the rate the targets were built on, so attainment gaps will keep widening while this holds.

points.what: For the week, orders reached 98.4% of target and revenue 89.6%.
points.so_what: Both measures were behind, and the wider revenue shortfall is the one that carries into the quarter position.

points.what: Quarter-to-date revenue is 87.7% of target, with $359,246 of the $774,555 quarterly target still outstanding and five weeks left.
points.so_what: The quarter is behind regardless of this week's order growth, and the amount left to cover is well above the recent weekly revenue pace.

points.what: Both completed and in-progress months are behind: Jan closed at 88.0% of target and Feb month-to-date stands at 87.2%.
points.so_what: The shortfall is consistent rather than a one-week event, which is what holds year-to-date attainment at 87.7%.

points.what: EMEA orders rose 27.1% to 164 and accounted for 37.6% of the week's order increase.
points.so_what: The largest single share of growth came from a mid-sized region, so the week's gain rests on a smaller base than APAC.

points.what: LATAM orders rose 32.1% to 107, contributing 26 of the 93 additional orders.
points.so_what: Together with EMEA, the smaller regions carried most of the week's order growth.

points.what: Search, at 69.6% of orders, grew 8.3% week on week and contributed 45.2% of the order increase.
points.so_what: The largest source grew more slowly than total orders of 13.4%, so the step up came disproportionately from smaller sources.

points.what: AOV was $83.51, down 0.2% on the prior week and up 0.5% on last year.
points.so_what: Revenue growth of 7.5% this week came from more orders, not from higher value per order.

points.what: The 14-Day Return Rate for the mature week of 02 Feb 2026 was 10.8%, down 0.8 pp on the previous week but 2.9 pp above last year.
points.so_what: Returns eased against the prior week yet remain above last year's level, so this is a measure to keep watching rather than one that has recovered.

points.what: Signups grew 5.1% year on year while orders grew 58.1%.
points.so_what: The two growth measures point in very different directions, so this year's order gain should not be read as signup-led.

points.what: Orders of 789 came in above the eight-week average of 707.
points.so_what: Volume ran ahead of the recent pace, yet still landed below the weekly target.

checks.name: 14-Day Return Rate names its mature week
anomaly flag acknowledged in the summary
sentences at most 30 words and 4 numbers
each slot only covers its allowed KPIs
